prerequisites.pedagogical_justification: The concept of a dynamic, changing magnetic field in this lecture builds upon passing an alternating current through a conductor.
Transformers cannot operate on DC; understanding AC is an absolute physical prerequisite to understanding why transformers work.
EMF (Faraday induction) is defined as the force pushing free electrons due to a changing magnetic field.
A transformer physically consists of primary and secondary coils sharing magnetic flux.
The fundamental operating principle of a transformer is mutual induction of electromotive force.
A step-up transformer is a specialized transformer; general transformer operating principles must be learned first.
A step-down transformer is a specialized transformer; general transformer operating principles must be learned first.
Voltage stepping is accomplished by varying the number of turns on the coil.
Three-phase transformers combine multiple single-phase transformers or use shared three-limb cores.
Delta and Y (Star) are specific topological wiring arrangements of a three-phase system.
